items.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024
items.q: a tenor sax player called — I think his name was Bob McCoy. And he was a contractor for Buddy Morrow’s band. And Buddy was looking for a lead player and they were going to offer me $175 a week if I would take it. And I thought $175, I’m making I think it was $150 then. So I took it.

ctx.x: What did you learn about human nature? This is a pretty broad question but in your travels with various bands did you learn anything about human nature that stuck with you?

You know not really. You know at that time I was young and just wanted to see the country and I was able to do that. I was actually being a professional in something I never thought I could do and then here I was doing it. So to me I was just out having a great © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

time, playing music that at the time I said if this is all I did the rest of my life — play this music — that’s all I’d ever want to do because the music was so much fun. I never played lead although the first time I was on Woody’s band I was playing like I said on one of the ends, Don was on the other end. And then Woody broke the band up because they just didn’t have any takers for booking the band at that time, so they disbanded the band. Bill Chase and Woody stayed on and they had a little quintet.
